lane: Local CPU gather/dense-equivalent comparison (synthetic qwen2moe fixture)
goal: Measure the merged-decode union gather against dense-equivalent solo stepping on identical sequences and token streams, prove bit-identical parity, and record the step's union active-expert amortization.
comparisonNotes: The fixture is synthetic deterministic F32 qwen2moe material: it measures the gather mechanism (union walks, slab views, prefetch staging), not a quantized production model.
Both arms run identical sequences and token streams over identical file bytes; parity compares every step's logits bit-for-bit between the merged-decode arm and solo stepping.

Union stats come from an instrumentation pass that counts slab resolutions through the gather kernel: unionGateResolutionsPerDecodeStep lists gate-role resolutions per decode step summed over the fixture's layers, while averages and byte tallies are reported per layer step — each distinct expert of a step's union resolves exactly one slab per role.

Substrate stream (linux o_direct+discard): expert role tensors resolve through cold whole-role reads into fresh buffers — unbuffered FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING transfers on Windows, sector-aligned O_DIRECT preads whose read range is released with posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED) on Linux (a buffered+discard descriptor when the filesystem refuses direct I/O) — while dense weights answer from ordinary buffered (OS-cached) reads so only expert traffic pays storage cost. Both arms pay this for their cold resolutions — the prefetch-only gather arm streams every union expert's roles, and a tier miss streams that expert chain's role tensors through the same slab-view route (the loader has no per-slab staging today); resident experts answer from private copies with zero streamed bytes.
